data.title: Arity to Acquire INRIX, Advancing a Connected Vision for the Future of Transportation
data.description:
Definitive agreement with INRIX marks an important step toward helping organizations create societal value by better understanding transportation

CHICAGO, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Arity, a subsidiary of The Allstate Corporation, announced today that it has entered into an agreement to acquire substantially all the assets of INRIX, a leading provider of transportation intelligence and mobility analytics. Expected to close in 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, the acquisition builds on Arity's role in advancing Allstate's investment in data, analytics, and mobility intelligence, leveraging more than three trillion miles of driving data to better understand how people, vehicles, and transportation systems move.

"Transportation operates as one connected system, yet the intelligence used to understand it remains fragmented across industries and data sources," said Gary Hallgren, president of Arity. "By combining Arity's predictive insights on driving behavior and risk with INRIX's transportation intelligence and mobility analytics, we will be uniquely positioned to deliver more robust intelligence and insights into how people, vehicles, goods, and roads interact. Just as important, we will bring together two talented teams with complementary expertise and a shared opportunity to shape the future of transportation systems. This acquisition advances our vision to help organizations understand what is happening today, anticipate the forces shaping what comes next, and make decisions that drive economic and societal value."

"For more than two decades, INRIX has helped customers make better transportation decisions through data, analytics, and transportation intelligence. Arity shares our vision that a complete understanding of how people, vehicles, roads, and goods interact can lead to better outcomes for our communities and businesses," said Bryan Mistele, co-founder and CEO of INRIX. "Combining INRIX's transportation intelligence with Arity's trillions of miles of mobility data and advanced analytics creates an opportunity to further innovate mobility intelligence and improve transportation effectiveness and efficiency for customers across the public and private sectors."

The transaction is an important part of Arity's broader vision to help organizations build a more complete understanding of transportation. By combining insights into driving behavior, mobility patterns, and roadway systems, Arity and INRIX can provide greater context for the decisions organizations make every day while helping them better anticipate change. Building on Arity's ongoing investments across the transportation ecosystem, the transaction expands the company's ability to help organizations better understand how transportation works and where it is headed.

From insurers managing risk and businesses moving goods to public agencies improving safety and planning infrastructure, better decisions increasingly depend on understanding transportation in a broader context. By bringing together complementary perspectives across behavior, movement, and roads, Arity is building intelligence that can help organizations see change earlier, act with greater confidence, and create safer, more resilient communities and economies.

About Arity

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chicago, Arity is a mobility data and analytics company and a subsidiary of The Allstate Corporation. Arity transforms trillions of miles of driving behavior data into intelligence that helps insurers, brands, and public-sector partners make smarter decisions across pricing, risk, marketing, and safety. Learn more at www.arity.com.

About INRIX

Founded in 2004, INRIX pioneered intelligent mobility solutions by transforming big data from connected devices and vehicles into mobility insights. INRIX has harnessed machine learning and artificial intelligence to deliver precise and actionable mobility data. This revolutionary approach enabled INRIX to become one of the leading providers of data and analytics in people and vehicle movement. With partners and solutions spanning across the mobility ecosystem, INRIX is uniquely positioned at the intersection of technology and transportation. Learn more at inrix.com.

data.title: September Industrial Production Rises More Than Forecast as Manufacturing Rebounds
data.description:
12:46 PM EDT, 10/16/2026 (MT Newswires) -- US industrial production increased more than expected in September as manufacturing output rebounded despite weakness in the auto component, Federal Reserve data showed Friday.

Industrial output grew 0.7% last month, following a revised 0.1% gain for August, according to the Fed. The consensus was for a smaller 0.4% increase in September in a survey compiled by Bloomberg.

Manufacturing production rose 0.3% last month, rebounding from a 0.2% decline in August and matching Wall Street's views.

Durable manufacturing output edged up 0.1% amid gains in primary metals, machinery, and electrical equipment, appliances, and components. Motor vehicles and parts dropped 3%, while the furniture category saw a 1.2% decline, according to Fed data.

Details of the report show bifurcation within the industry, Oxford Economics said.

"Many durable goods sectors are riding the coattails of the (artificial intelligence) buildout and higher defense spending, while others exposed to housing are struggling," Oxford Economics Deputy Chief US Economist Bernard Yaros said in a note e-mailed to MT Newswires.

The firm doesn't expect the weakness in auto production to persist ahead, as high-income consumers continue to benefit from growing wealth, while "spillovers from the broader recovery in industrial demand supports demand for heavy duty trucks," Yaros wrote.

Mining output increased 0.2% in September, while utilities grew 3.5%, with the electric component rising 3.7% and natural gas up 2.1%, Fed data showed.

"The near-term forecast for industrial production will get revised higher on the back of this report, and we still maintain our view that next year will be even stronger," Yaros said. "Key drivers such as AI and defense will prove durable to the risks posed by higher long-term yields and the energy shock."

Earlier this month, separate surveys by the Institute for Supply Management and S&P Global ( SPGI ) showed that the US manufacturing sector continued to expand in September amid robust demand and growth in employment, though inflationary pressures remained a key concern.

data.title: US regional banks join bigger peers in signaling resilient economy as lending holds firm
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - A clutch of US regional banks reported strong third-quarter earnings this week, powered by robust loan demand from businesses, adding to signs that the economy remained resilient despite rising borrowing costs.

Earlier in the week, the biggest US banks such as JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Citigroup ( C ) also reported higher loan balances, even as weakness in the capital markets hit their investment banking revenue.

People have accepted global uncertainty as the new normal and are pushing forward with operations, PNC Financial CEO William Demchak said.

"The clouds are as dark as they ever were, but the economy's still strong. People are investing into it," Demchak added.

PNC led the regional banks' loan growth at 14.2% in the third quarter, followed by U.S. Bancorp ( USB ) at 8%, M&T Bank ( MTB ) at 5.5% and Citizens Financial ( CFG ) at 5.29%.

The robust borrowing activity defied rising expectations that still-high inflation fueled by the Iran war and the Federal Reserve's September interest rate hike could chill corporate capital expenditures and dampen borrowing appetite.

Top regional banking executives said loan pipelines remained strong and they had not seen any slowdown yet in demand.

Citizens Financial ( CFG ) said loan demand actually started to pick up in the last couple of weeks as the bank entered the fourth quarter.

AI CATALYST?

Banking executives said they were looking to understand how much of the loan growth was linked to the massive AI-related spending when pressed by analysts during post-earnings sessions.

"This whole AI ecosystem build-out is kind of full-on. It's a very strong dynamic, and that kind of cascades into a lot of the supply ecosystem," Citizens Financial ( CFG ) CEO Bruce Van Saun said.

"Even with higher rates, the kind of desire to get the compute power in place, the players aren't really batting an eyelash," he added.

PNC, which does not have a large data-center finance business, said there is an impact from the AI spending boom on tangential sectors like heavy equipment, transportation and energy.

"If the capex broadly slows down related to AI, do we think, even though we don't lend directly to that, it would slower loan growth? Yes, I do," PNC's Demchak said.

Some regional banks downplayed the AI dependency and emphasized broad-based commercial and industrial loan growth.

U.S. Bancorp CFO John Stern said loan growth was robust even outside AI-adjacent sectors, highlighting areas like retail, food and beverage, and insurance.

(Reporting by Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Sriraj Kalluvila)

data.title: First Horizon's Loan Restructuring Enhances Strategic Flexibility, UBS Says
data.description:
12:57 PM EDT, 10/16/2026 (MT Newswires) -- First Horizon's ( FHN ) restructuring of $4.5 billion in residential loans in Q3 is expected to strengthen the bank's franchise and keep several strategic paths open, including remaining independent, UBS Securities said Thursday in a report.

The move improves the bank's positioning by cleaning up old accounting adjustments tied to the loans, which had made the balance sheet harder for investors or a potential buyer to assess, the report said.

The restructuring reduces the accounting burden for any future acquirer by nearly a third, even though it also lowers the potential takeout value, UBS said. Management also indicated it is no longer interested in pursuing a small acquisition, the report said.

The transaction comes at a cost as UBS estimates roughly 5% tangible book value dilution and an earnback period closer to seven years, assuming loan growth picks up after nearly three years of softness. The restructuring also makes First Horizon ( FHN ) more sensitive to rising interest rates and improves loan profitability by about 75 basis points, the firm said.

Pre-provision net revenue in Q3 missed UBS's expectations, and the outlook still depends heavily on deposit pricing, where First Horizon ( FHN ) has trailed peers. The bank's more asset-sensitive balance sheet should help over time, though the magnitude of improvement will hinge on how deposit costs evolve, the report said.

UBS maintained its neutral rating on First Horizon ( FHN ) stock and its $26 price target.

data.title: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
data.description:
PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island/NEW YORK, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A sharp decline in CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.

Analysts and portfolio managers said the selloff in the data center operator's debt carries more significance than a concurrent rout in its shares because it may signal a broader reassessment of the risks tied to financing AI projects that may take years to generate revenue.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds issued in June at a yield of 9.675% have plunged in value, sending their yield to 15% this week.

"CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is absolutely the canary in the coal mine" for a market segment that is coming under more stress, said Max Frumes, global head of distressed and leveraged finance at 9fin, a fintech corporate credit data and analytics company.

"This is going to be a turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom," said Frumes, who believes that other AI-linked debt will follow CoreWeave ( CRWV ) into distressed territory. "It's going to get more expensive. There will be a lot more scrutiny and probably some pushback from investors."

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares fell 15.1% from Monday's open through Thursday's close, despite a 6% gain on Thursday after a vote of confidence from partner Nvidia. The decline was broadly in line with weakness in other so-called neocloud companies such as Nebius and Iren.

Credit investors said they already are becoming more selective.

"We're definitely taking another look at our exposures across the AI infrastructure space, particularly where the risks are concentrated and whether we're being adequately compensated for taking them," said John Han, a portfolio manager at fixed-income asset management firm F/m Investments.

F/m's portfolio contains unsecured CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds in one of its exchange-traded funds, but only because they make up part of the index tracked by the ETF. At their current yields those bonds "certainly deserve another look," Han said. He generally prefers to invest in high-yield securities via special purpose vehicles that may offer lower yields but also more collateral and less risk.

"The market is being very selective and really singling out anything that has more leverage, and (that may be) in a bit more challenging operating environment," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager of fixed income at Catalyst funds.

To Holzenthaler and other investors, what the markets are witnessing now is an overreaction as sentiment shifts from being overly upbeat to downright bearish.

In June, the risks driving the selloff -- the sheer size of the funding needs, the leverage, the reliance on outside financing, the risk that the GPUs (graphics processing units) being purchased for data centers would be obsolete before the new facilities could open -- were merely overlooked or downplayed.

"A few months ago, I would have said people were just too optimistic around AI," Holzenthaler said.

Deutsche Bank global head of macro and thematic research Jim Reid sees the market entering a new phase in which debt financing is becoming increasingly important.

"As we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," Reid wrote in a recent report. "AI financing costs aren't dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges."

Vanguard bond portfolio manager Brad Collins said assessing AI-related debt has become more challenging as issuers bring increasingly large and varied offerings to market, often forcing investors to make decisions in days or even hours.

Rising inflation has pushed financing costs higher overall and fueled concern about what lies ahead for mammoth AI capital spending plans. Then there is the growing political controversy surrounding the construction of data centers.

Even one of the tech sector's stalwarts allows that the road ahead may be bumpy at times. Dan Ives, partner and technology analyst at Yorkville Ives, an investment firm, estimates that 5% to 10% of planned projects ultimately will not be built.

"The growing noise around data center permitting and midterm rhetoric on power prices has given investors another reason to step back," Ives said.

(Reporting by Suzanne McGee in Providence, Rhode Island and Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss in New York; editing by Colin Barr and Cynthia Osterman)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks edge lower as dollar heads for weekly loss
data.description:
* US dollar heads for weekly loss on lower US Treasury yields

* Bond markets stabilise after rush for safe havens on Thursday

* Investors worry about debt risks in AI-related stocks

(Updates headline and prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Elizabeth Howcroft and Chibuike Oguh

NEW YORK/PARIS, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Global stocks edged lower on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.

Markets have been rattled this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks.

Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds.

On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was flat but set for a weekly gain.

Technology and communication services were driving losses while top gainers were utilities and consumer staples stocks.

CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) shares shed 9% on the day and were on track to lose nearly 23% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.01%, the S&P 500 fell 0.61%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.3%.

The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.10% and was set for a weekly loss. European stock indexes, hit less hard by Thursday's selloff, were higher, with the STOXX 600 up 0.67%. London's FTSE 100 rose 0.38%.

"We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund, said.

"Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues."

Asian stocks mostly rose and bond markets steadied on Friday, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves.

Indonesian equities suffered their biggest drop since 1998 after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds.

DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER

The dollar index fell 0.23% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, analysts said.

The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.10% at $1.1232.

The Japanese yen strengthened 0.04% against the greenback to 157.92 per dollar.

European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields fell. Germany's 10-year yield rose 0.14 basis point to 3.411%. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 0.17 basis points to 5.085%.

Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May.

Brent crude futures rose 0.85% to $106.83 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged in the past 10 days.

Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.17% to about $4,177.14 an ounce.

(Reporting by Kevin Buckland and Elizabeth Howcroft; Editing by Ros Russell, Mark Potter and Andrew Heavens)

data.title: Judge rejects CFTC, Gemini bid to vacate $5 million settlement

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A federal judge in Manhattan has rejected a joint request by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Gemini, a cryptocurrency exchange founded by twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, to undo a $5 million settlement from the Biden administration. 

In a ruling on Thursday, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein said the agency and Gemini Trust Co had not met the standards required to set aside the settlement, which resolved a lawsuit over statements Gemini made during the agency's review of a proposed bitcoin futures contract.

The CFTC and a lawyer for Gemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The CFTC sued Gemini in 2022, alleging the company made false or misleading statements during the agency's review of the proposed futures product. The January 2025 settlement came at the end of Democratic President Joe Biden's administration and shortly before a trial.

Republican President Donald Trump's administration has taken a friendlier, narrower approach to crypto sector enforcement.

The commodities agency and Gemini in May jointly asked Hellerstein, appointed by Democratic President Bill Clinton, to wipe out the settlement and court order. They said in a filing that the agency's complaint, lodged in 2022, would not have been filed under new enforcement policy priorities and standards under Trump.

The court filing said regulators should not ​have accused Gemini of making false statements in connection with ​its bitcoin futures business. The CFTC and Gemini said the CFTC had "resorted to inappropriate tactics" to bring a lawsuit.

Gemini ⁠agreed not to receive a refund on the $5 million penalty if the settlement were vacated.

Hellerstein said Gemini had litigated against the CFTC for more than three years before voluntarily agreeing to settle and that the agency's current view of the case does not require vacating the settlement.

The Winklevoss twins became widely known after accusing Mark Zuckerberg of stealing their idea for Facebook, a dispute that ended with a 2008 settlement that included cash and company stock.

data.title: Analysis-Indonesia faces rare MSCI exclusion that could cut it off from global capital
data.description:
SINGAPORE/HONG KONG/LONDON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A warning from MSCI that it may exclude Indonesia from its stock market indexes - benchmarks used by global financial investors - risks cutting the nation off from international capital and relegating it to an investment backwater.

MSCI stunned investors by proposing that it remove Indonesia from its global stock indexes altogether, months after floating a less severe downgrade from emerging market to frontier over opaque ownership and securities trading practices.

A cut to standalone status would be unusually harsh and rare: Argentina was dropped in 2021 for imposing capital controls, and Russia in 2022 after Western sanctions cut it off from global finance over its invasion of Ukraine. Indonesia would find itself in a small group of standalone markets that includes Lebanon and Zimbabwe.

Indonesia has been an MSCI emerging market since 1989, and a downgrade of the proposed magnitude would be a huge reversal for a market that until recently was a foreign investor favourite.

Removing the country from major global benchmarks that steer billions of dollars in foreign investment could hurt far more than just its stock market. 

"The proposal ... goes well beyond what we had considered our worst-case scenario," said Rully Arya Wisnubroto, head of research at Mirae Asset Sekuritas in Jakarta.

The MSCI announcement wiped about $65 billion off the value of Indonesian equities, with an 11.6% drop on the Jakarta Composite Index - its biggest one-day fall since the Asian financial crisis in 1998.

The shock spread beyond equities, with the rupiah falling as much as 0.8% and some analysts raising the possibility of a central bank interest rate hike on Tuesday, when rates had been expected to stay on hold.

"The purpose (of a rate hike) would be pre-emptive, i.e. in order to prevent the expected equity foreign outflows from widening to the fixed income side as well as being exacerbated by resident capital outflows," Citi wrote in a note to clients.

Unlike a downgrade to frontier status, a move to standalone would provide no offsetting demand from frontier-index funds, leaving passive emerging-market money heading for the exits.

Banks estimate the move could trigger $3 billion to $6 billion in passive outflows, with JPMorgan putting the figure at $4.8 billion and UBS warning active investors could pull another $15 billion.

More than $1.8 trillion in assets are benchmarked to MSCI's emerging-market indexes, according to the index provider's website.

INDONESIA INDEX WEIGHT AMPLIFIES IMPACT 

Indonesia, Southeast Asia's biggest economy, is the world's top exporter of thermal coal, palm oil ​and nickel and a major supplier of copper and coffee. While the country has benefited from rising prices of some ‌of its ⁠top commodity exports this year, as a net oil importer, its import bills have also soared. 

The fallout from the stock index exclusion could also spread to Indonesia's public finances should state-linked companies find it harder or more expensive to raise money, potentially forcing the government to take spending back onto its own books or scale back investment, Citi analysts added. 

"We expect the broader economic impact to be predominantly indirect, with external financing representing the most immediate transmission channel," said Irman Faiz, economist at Bank Danamon Indonesia in Jakarta.

Indonesia's removal would involve significantly more index-linked money than previous cases, despite its weight shrinking from 1.2% at the end of 2025 to 0.46% now, according to JPMorgan. When Argentina was removed, its weighting stood at 0.12%.

"Is Indonesia really on par with Zimbabwe in market behaviour and structure? Is shareholder treatment really worse than in many other EM markets, including several in Asia?" said Juan Torres, co-manager of the Neuberger Emerging Markets Equity fund.

MSCI cited opaque ownership, suspected coordinated trading and inadequate enforcement, saying the problems undermine investors' ability to determine companies' true free float and rely on market prices.

The index provider expects the downgrade to go ahead unless a consultation running until next April finds clear evidence of improved governance and market functioning. A final decision is due by next June.

Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats. On Friday, the regulator also announced sanctions linked to alleged manipulation in three stocks.

"It's true that MSCI has a strong reputation, and it's also true that we need to pay attention to what they say," said Dradjad Hari Wibowo, the deputy coordinating minister for economic affairs. "But there's one thing I want to emphasize - they (MSCI) aren't always right."

(Reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore, Yantoultra Ngui in Hong Kong and Karin Strohecker in London; Additional reporting by Stefanno Sulaiman and Johann M Cherian; Writing by Tom Westbrook and Karin Strohecker; Editing by Hugh Lawson)

data.title: Analysis-SpaceX's spectrum deal still leaves it far from rivaling telecom giants
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.

Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder.

Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections.

The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions - costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T ( T ), Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations.

Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory.

"It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished."

Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers.

"There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy.

SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN

SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service.

"Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase.

SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops - a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone - it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week.

In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service.

SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said.

SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said.

Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat.

T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Peter Henderson and Joyjeet Das)

data.title: KFC picks Coca-Cola as US soda supplier, ditches longtime partner PepsiCo (Oct 15)
data.description:
* Coca-Cola products to reach KFC's ( YUM ) 3,718 US restaurants by spring 2027

* Financial details of KFC's ( YUM ) US beverage partnership with Coca-Cola are not disclosed

* PepsiCo ( PEP ) says it renewed beverage agreements across Taco Bell and KFC International stores

By Juveria Tabassum

Oct 15 (Reuters) - Fast-food chain KFC ( YUM ) on Thursday signed Coca-Cola as its beverage partner for US stores, bringing to a close a relationship with PepsiCo ( PEP ) that dates back about four decades.

The loss of the beverage partnership with KFC ( YUM ), which has 3,718 US locations, could be a setback for PepsiCo ( PEP ) as it works to improve soda sales in the country, while its snacks business grapples with high prices and a shift to healthier options.

Higher costs have also added to concerns for PepsiCo ( PEP ) CEO Ramon Laguarta, who said earlier this month that growth and margin recovery was taking longer than planned.

The partnership began when PepsiCo ( PEP ) acquired KFC ( YUM ) in a bid to expand into food and snacks. While PepsiCo ( PEP ) later spun off KFC ( YUM ) in 1997, it continued to be a beverage partner for its parent Yum Brands ( YUM ).

"It is just a bad look for PepsiCo ( PEP )... when you lose a big-name brand partner like that. This could be the optical straw that breaks the camel's back," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets.

"It is very rare that you have two giants in the same industry take such a different turn," he said. Freedom Capital Markets holds shares in Coca-Cola.

PepsiCo ( PEP ) is also under scrutiny from activist investor Elliott Investment Management, which disclosed a stake in the company last year, and has asked it to sell underperforming assets and improve its performance in North America.

Yum Brands ( YUM ) and PepsiCo ( PEP ) just renewed agreements across Taco Bell and KFC International stores, a spokesperson for PepsiCo ( PEP ) told Reuters. Taco Bell is a 10-year agreement, they said.

PepsiCo ( PEP ) has beverage partner agreements at sandwich chains Subway and Jersey Mike's Subs. It also runs the soda fountain at Pizza Hut, which left the Yum Brands ( YUM ) umbrella only this year and switched to PepsiCo ( PEP ) from Coca-Cola in 2011.

Coca-Cola products will be available at KFC US restaurants by spring 2027, the company said. Financial details of the partnership were not disclosed.

Coca-Cola is a long-standing beverage partner at burger chains McDonald's and Wendy's.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

data.title: NY Fed service sector survey finds notable price pressures
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - Service sector business leaders reported widespread pricing woes in October and a downbeat outlook for activity, according to a report released Friday by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

"The pace of input price increases remained sharp, and selling price increases picked up to the fastest pace since 2022," the bank said in its latest Business Leaders Survey for the current month, adding "supply availability continued to worsen."

The price pressures faced by the company leaders came as the report found that the business climate was "much worse than normal" with firms becoming more pessimistic about the outlook. Current business activity also weakened, with the headline index dropping 12 points to negative 20.7, the weakest reading since March, the report said.

The sour mood captured by the New York Fed survey contrasts with other data that shows strong economic activity, low and steady unemployment and robust levels of investment tied to the technology sector.

That said, the survey's downbeat findings on inflation mirror a raft of statistics showing price pressures remain strong amid the ongoing impact of President Donald Trump's trade tariffs and the US-Israeli war in the Middle East that's driven surging energy costs.

High inflation drove the Fed to hike rates last month and it's very likely to do so again by year's end, though in comments late Thursday, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh offered no guidance, saying "I don't prejudge meetings...I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."

Chicago Fed leader Austan Goolsbee, in a Yahoo Finance interview on Wednesday, said a consumer level inflation report released on Wednesday was "discouraging" and noted "if you break out the components, services inflation shows little sign of improvement."

"We're going to need to keep a close eye" on that part of the price pressure landscape "because that's not really coming from supply shocks," Goolsbee said.

The NY Fed survey pointing to rough price pressures came as the government reported a surge in import prices in September, with those costs rising by a much bigger than expected 1.1% rate.

The Business Leaders survey also pointed to "weak" capital spending plans and while noting "supply availability is expected to continue to worsen."

The sour turn in the October Business Leaders survey, joined with other regional data from the bank, points to an uneven environment in the New York area. The bank's October Empire State factory survey, released Thursday, saw the overall business conditions index rise to its highest level in five years amid "elevated" input and selling prices and supply-related challenges.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama )

data.title: US manufacturing output rises in September
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - US factory production increased in September, but lost considerable momentum in the third quarter amid headwinds from the Middle East conflict, which has snarled supply chains and raised energy prices. 

Manufacturing output rebounded 0.3% last month following a revised 0.2% decline in August, the Federal Reserve said on Friday. The rise was in line with economists' expectations. Factory production was previously estimated to have dropped 0.3% in August. Output advanced 1.1% on a year-over-year basis in September. It grew at a 0.7% annualized rate in the third quarter after accelerating at a 5.6% pace in the second quarter.

Manufacturing accounts for about 9.4% of the economy. While an AI infrastructure buildout and businesses rebuilding inventories to meet robust domestic demand are supporting factory activity, higher energy prices, a trade war with Canada and rising borrowing costs pose downside risks to production. 

Diesel prices have surged to a record high as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on, and economists say the economy could soon feel the effects through higher prices for goods, including at the supermarket, which could weigh on demand.

Durable goods manufacturing production edged up 0.1%, lifted by gains in the output of primary metals, machinery, and electrical equipment, appliances and components. Production of motor vehicles and parts fell 3.0%. Durable goods manufacturing output increased at a 3.8% rate in the third quarter, partly boosted by a 28.4% surge in the production of semiconductors and related electronic components related to the AI spending boom.

Nondurable manufacturing production rose 0.4% over the month amid gains in printing and chemicals output. Nondurable manufacturing output, however, fell 1.6% last quarter.  

Mining production rose 0.2% last month and grew at a 5.0% rate in the July-September quarter. Utilities jumped 3.5% amid demand for air-conditioning. Utilities output increased at a 14.8% pace in the third quarter.

Overall industrial production rose 0.7% last month after gaining 0.1% in August. Industrial output increased 2.2% year-on-year in September. It advanced at a 2.8% pace in the third quarter after growing at a 4.8% rate in the second quarter.

Capacity utilization for the industrial sector, a measure of how fully firms are using their resources, rose to 76.9% last month from 76.4% in August. It is 2.5 percentage points below its 1972-2025 average. The operating rate for the manufacturing sector edged up to 75.9% from 75.8% in August. It is 2.3 percentage points below its long-run average.

(Reporting by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Andrea Ricci )
